title_en: New ETF Launches & the Rise of AI in China
title_zh: VettaFi 的 Kirsten Chang 与 EMXETF 的 Kevin Carter 谈新 ETF 发行潮与中国 AI 的崛起
subtitle_zh: 破纪录的 ETF 发行年、AI 债务与费率战，再到中国 AI 五层技术栈的拆解。
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Prime 由主持 Nate Geraci 坐镇，分两段对话。前半程请来 VettaFi 高级行业分析师 Kirsten Chang，盘点创纪录的新 ETF 发行年：今年以来已有 1218 只 ETF 发行，资产合计约 1230 亿美元，其中 46 只单只资产已超 5 亿美元，说明市场空白（white space）依然存在。两人逐一拆解几只新品：Schwab 以 6 个基点（bps）发行 SCIN、Corgi Invest 一口气推出 14 只费率低至 2 个基点的债券 ETF，显示核心固定收益的费率战尚未结束；但 VettaFi 研讨会调查显示，近 59% 的顾问最看重投资策略、26.5% 看重管理人业绩，费率只占不到 12%。他们还谈到 AI 基础设施债 ETF（AIBN）、ProShares 的 hyperscaler 债 ETF、带杠杆的 CDS ETF 申报、Sequoia 近 70 亿美元的共同基金转 ETF（SEQ）、VanEck 的全合一 WBMO，以及 Canary 的 Staked Injective ETF（INJC）。后半程请来 EMQQ Global 与 EMXETF 创始人兼 CIO Kevin Carter，他用「五层 AI 蛋糕」拆解中国 AI 技术栈（AICH、TGRZ、EMAG）：中国在电力上明显领先，芯片受制于 ASML 与 TSMC，而开源大模型已拿下美国约 63% 的 token 份额；TSMC、Samsung、SK Hynix 三家今明两年合计将赚到 1.2 万亿美元利润，接近新兴市场指数三分之一的权重。信息密度极高，是理解 2026 年 ETF 发行潮与中国 AI 投资价值的实用一课。

turns.zh: 让这些公司可以继续设立他们已有的数据中心。但那上面压着很多钱，很多美国公司都在重投同一类业务模式。所以 Alice 在这类事情上并不是孤身一人。

turns.en: So, with the China AI ETFs, I mean, do you view these as, I think I know how you'll answer this, but are these to diversify US AI exposure or the view to the hedge? Like, how should people think about these in the context of a portfolio?
turns.zh: 那么，这些中国 AI ETF，我是说，你会怎么看待它们——我大概知道你会怎么回答——它们是用来分散美国 AI 敞口的，还是被看作一种对冲（hedge）？人们应该如何在组合的语境里思考这些产品？

turns.en: Well, I look, we made these because we thought they should exist, right? There are two superpowers for AI. The US has 100 ETFs that track in different ways. Some of them pretty watered down, frankly. But we wanted to create a pure play version for people to get the exposure. It's sure, maybe you could think it was a hedge.
turns.zh: 嗯，你看，我们做这些产品，是因为我们认为它们应该存在，对吧？AI 只有两个超级大国，而美国有 100 只 ETF 在用不同的方式跟踪它，坦白说其中有些已经稀释得很厉害。但我们想做一个纯正的版本，让人们拿到这个敞口。当然，你可以把它当成一种对冲，

turns.en: You could think of it as a way, you know, if you're a more enterprising speculative investor, you're right, to play this different part of the world's AI, you know, existence, right? I mean, AI is here. Now, look, to be frank, all of this is incredibly risky. I mean, this, these, especially the tigers at AICH, these might be the most risky investment products that are unlevered out there.
turns.zh: 也可以把它看作一种方式，如果你是一个更进取、更投机的投资者，你可以用它去参与世界另一端的 AI 版图，对吧？我是说，AI 就在这里。好吧，坦白讲，所有这些都是极高风险的。我是说，这些产品，尤其是 TGRZ 和 AICH，可能是市面上不带杠杆的产品里风险最高的。

turns.en: Right? And especially if you measure risk by volatility, which technically, if you use Greek letters, that is what you're defining risk as is volatility. So these are high volatility, high risk products to be sure. Now, AICH is full of many very profitable companies.
turns.zh: 对吧？尤其是如果你用波动率来衡量风险——从技术上讲，如果你用希腊字母那套方法，风险被定义的就是波动率。所以这些确实是高波动、高风险的产品。当然，AICH 里面有很多非常赚钱的公司，

turns.en: Alibaba tends that these are incredibly profitable and very cheap companies, the hardware companies in that stack that the Chinese companies making GPUs, making optical components, very profitable companies, when you get to the large language models, the tigers, these companies are not making money.
turns.zh: Alibaba、Tencent 这些公司极其盈利、估值又非常便宜；技术栈里的硬件公司，那些做 GPU、做光模块的中国公司，也是非常赚钱的。但当你走到大语言模型、走到 Tigers 这一层，这些公司是不赚钱的。

turns.en: There's, we don't know if they'll ever make money. And ultimately, while, you know, I'm putting together these products, I think about everything in a very simple, you know, Omaha sort of thinking, right? The reason companies have value is to make profits.
turns.zh: 我们不知道它们将来会不会赚钱。归根结底，在搭建这些产品的时候，我是用一种非常简单的、奥马哈式（Omaha）的思考方式来看一切的，对吧？公司之所以有价值，是因为它能创造利润，

turns.en: The only way to grow the value is to grow the profits. And if your buying companies that don't make any profits by definition, these are speculative investments. And so TGRZ, again, is about as risky of an investment as you can make. It's heavily concentrated into two Chinese large language models that, while they are growing fast and generating revenue, they don't have a profit, which is also the case for most of our AI.
turns.zh: 而增值的唯一途径就是让利润增长。如果你买的是根本不产生利润的公司，那么从定义上讲，这些就是投机性投资。所以再说一次，TGRZ 大概是你能做的风险最高的投资之一，它高度集中在两家中国大语言模型公司上，虽然它们增长很快、也在产生收入，但它们没有利润——这对我们大多数的 AI 公司来说也是一样的情况。

turns.en: Well, and I'll just add to that and we have just a few minutes left here, but I have this theory that AI models are basically commodities and that these are all just hardware and code and energy.
turns.zh: 嗯，我补充一点，我们只剩几分钟了。我有一个理论：AI 模型基本上就是大宗商品（commodities），它们都只是硬件、代码和能源。

turns.en: And the models are, I use this kind of air quotes very easily replicated over time in that if you have one AI model that has significant advances. And let's say that's a Chinese, you know, open source model.
turns.zh: 而这些模型，我这里要打上引号，随着时间推移是很容易被复制的。也就是说，如果你有一个 AI 模型取得了重大进展，假设那是一个中国的开源模型，

turns.en: Then other competing models are going to quickly catch up. And so I just think differentiation is going to be extremely difficult across that space longer term, which that means what individuals and businesses are going to be willing to pay for AI will ultimately grind toward the marginal cost of production.
turns.zh: 那么其他竞争模型会很快追上来。所以我觉得长期来看，这个领域里的差异化会极其困难，这意味着个人和企业愿意为 AI 支付的价格，最终会被磨向生产的边际成本（marginal cost of production）。

turns.en: You have any quick thoughts on that and maybe what that might mean for investing in the space. Maybe that's a little bit what you were alluding to in terms of the risks. Look, I think ultimately there are lots of products that are essentially commodities that in other sectors, you know, that you can find a way to make money at, right?
turns.zh: 你对这一点有什么快速的想法吗？也许这对投资这个领域意味着什么——也许这正是你刚才暗示的那些风险。看，我觉得归根结底，有很多产品本质上就是大宗商品，而在其他行业里，你照样能找到赚钱的办法，对吧？

turns.en: A hamburger. There's a lot of people making money in the hamburger business. There's a burrito, you know, a multi-billion dollar burrito company. So if you can add value or give customers something they want from and you should be able to sell it for more than cost you to make it, right?
turns.zh: 汉堡，做汉堡生意的人里有很多在赚钱。还有 burrito，有一家市值几十亿美元的 burrito 公司。所以如果你能增加价值，或者给客户提供他们想要的东西，你就应该能以高于成本的价格卖出去，对吧？

turns.en: And it doesn't really matter what sector it's been, but there doesn't seem to be a real clear moat like you have perhaps in in other kind of consumer companies and other companies. So you could be right. There's a lot of people share your opinion. It seems to me that what I understand is that the models we have today are good enough.
turns.zh: 而且这跟是哪个行业其实没什么关系。但这里似乎并不存在一条真正清晰的护城河（moat），不像你在其他消费类公司或者其他类型公司里看到的那样。所以你可能说得对，很多人和你持同样的观点。在我看来，我理解的情况是，我们今天的模型已经足够好了，

turns.en: But as as Nundin Nilkani, the great Indian tech leader has said they can stop working on the models for 10 years and it's not going to change anything because the models we have already are so powerful. It's a lot more about actually using them and figuring out how to deploy them than getting the next, you know, frontier model.
turns.zh: 但就像那位伟大的印度科技领袖 Nandan Nilekani 说过的，他们可以在模型上停止研究 10 年，也不会有任何改变，因为我们已有的模型已经足够强大了。现在更重要的其实是真正去使用它们、弄清楚怎么部署它们，而不是去拿下一个前沿模型。

turns.en: And thus again, like the China models have taken so much market share or token share in the last year. So real quick, before I let you go, that 30 TF is the, it's under the EMX ETF umbrella, right?
turns.zh: 所以再一次，就像中国模型在过去一年里拿走了那么多的市场份额、那么多的 token 份额。好，在我放你走之前，很快问一下，那只第三 ETF 是在 EMXETF 这个品牌下面，对吧？

turns.en: Launched just a few weeks ago, the emerging markets, AI mag 3 ETF to go e mag and this offer is exposure to Taiwan semiconductor Samsung and SK high next. That's it, just those three companies. So yeah, tell us the idea behind that ETF.
turns.zh: 就在几周前发行的，新兴市场 AI Mag 3 ETF，代码 EMAG，它提供的是对 TSMC、Samsung 和 SK Hynix 的敞口。就这三家，仅此而已。那么，跟我们讲讲这只 ETF 背后的思路吧。

turns.en: Okay, so if you look at what's happened in emerging markets since January of last year, they have been on fire as an asset class, the emerging market index from MSCI, which the I shares funds track.
turns.zh: 好，如果你看去年 1 月以来新兴市场发生了什么，作为一个资产类别它们一直在熊熊燃烧。MSCI 的新兴市场指数，也就是 iShares 那些基金跟踪的指数，

turns.en: It's up basically twice as much as the S&P in the last 22 months, but it's almost all of that has been driven by those three companies because they are the picks and shovels providers.
turns.zh: 在过去 22 个月里的涨幅基本上是 S&P 的两倍，但几乎全部的涨幅都是由那三家公司驱动的，因为它们是「卖铲子」的供应商。

turns.en: Within the AI story, the investment story, there's four or five trillion dollar questions. One question, of course, is can anthropic and open AI or the Chinese Tigers ever make a profit to more their valuation? Will the hyperscalers ever make a return on the trillions of investment? I don't know the answer to those.
turns.zh: 在 AI 这个故事、这个投资故事里，有四五个万亿美元级别的问题。第一个问题当然是：Anthropic 和 OpenAI，或者中国的 Tigers，究竟能不能赚到利润？第二个是它们的估值。超大规模云厂商到底能不能从数万亿美元的投资里拿到回报？这些问题我不知道答案。

turns.en: But all of that negative cash cash flow is piling up as profits for the mag 3 people don't realize those three companies have had one of the greatest financial windfalls in industrial history when people realize last year that the data centers are coming and we just don't have enough hardware to fill them up.
turns.zh: 但所有那些负现金流，都在变成 Mag 3 的利润堆积起来。人们没有意识到，这三家公司正在经历工业史上最伟大的财务横财之一。当去年人们意识到数据中心要来、而我们根本没有足够的硬件去填满它们时，

turns.en: And there's a supply demand imbalance. There's way too much demand because historically those companies were making parts for smartphones for the emerging market consumer to buy a cheap Android smartphone.
turns.zh: 供需失衡就出现了：需求太多太多。因为在历史上，这些公司做的是给智能手机供货的零部件，供新兴市场的消费者去买一部便宜的 Android 手机。

turns.en: And so their revenue was a little lumpy. It was growing, but it wasn't really impressive growth. But now there's this huge new demand and those three companies have quadrupled their revenue and their profits are mind boggling.
turns.zh: 所以他们的收入有点起伏不定，是在增长，但算不上令人惊艳的增长。而现在出现了这个巨大的新需求，这三家公司的收入翻了四倍，利润高得令人难以置信。

turns.en: Between this year and next year, they're going to make 1.2 trillion dollars of profit, 1.2 trillion of profit, which is about one and a half times the amount of profit Berkshire half the ways ever made.
turns.zh: 今年加明年，他们要赚到 1.2 万亿美元的利润，1.2 万亿美元的利润，这大约是 Berkshire Hathaway 有史以来赚到的利润总和的 1.5 倍。

turns.en: It's more than four times the lifetime profits of Amazon. So we can be worried about the hyperscalers, but if you want to see where their cash is piling up, it's in Korea and Taiwan. And again, they've driven this year about 90% of the emerging market return is just those three stocks.
turns.zh: 这比 Amazon 有史以来的累计利润还要多四倍以上。所以我们可以去担心那些超大规模云厂商，但如果你想知道他们的现金都堆到哪儿去了，答案就是韩国和台湾。而且再说一次，今年新兴市场回报里大约 90% 就是这三只股票贡献的。

turns.en: So when I was deconstructing AI in emerging markets, those three companies, they sit in a very high position. They're now a third of the entire emerging markets index and they remain very cheap. What do you think the P.E. multiple is for SK high necks if you had to guess?
turns.zh: 所以当我在拆解新兴市场的 AI 时，这三家公司处在非常高的位置。它们现在占整个新兴市场指数的三分之一，而且估值仍然非常便宜。你猜 SK Hynix 的市盈率（P.E.）倍数是多少？

turns.en: Okay, we talked about it. People, I'll let people go check and see what it is, but I've asked a lot of people and most of them are way off the mark when they guess what is the P.E. multiple for the Mag 3.
turns.zh: 好，我们聊过这个。我会让大家自己去查一查是多少，但我问过很多人，他们猜 Mag 3 的市盈率倍数时，大多数都错得离谱。

turns.en: So these are big companies. They're stacking cash and their valuations are somewhat surprising. And it's one of the other trillion dollar questions. So I'll leave it at that.
turns.zh: 所以这些都是大公司，他们在不断堆积现金，而他们的估值多少有点出人意料。这也是那几个万亿美元级问题中的另一个。所以我就说到这里。

turns.en: Yeah, the only counter to that, which I'll throw out there is, and you know, this in chips, you know, semi's or semi's, it's highly cyclical. And so, you know, some people may look ahead. I'm just saying and say that there's a lot of expectations baked into.
turns.zh: 是啊，我唯一想抛出来的反驳是——你知道，这在芯片里，半导体就是强周期（highly cyclical）行业。所以有些人可能会往前看，我只是说，这里面已经计入了大量的预期，

turns.en: Especially forward earnings expectations. And so we start looking at P.E.s. Again, there's a lot of expectations in there. That would be the counter.
turns.zh: 尤其是前瞻盈利的预期。所以当我们开始看市盈率时，再说一次，里面已经包含了非常多的预期。这算是反驳意见。

turns.en: Well, and I'm familiar with that counter. And what I would say is it is absolutely 100% true that historically these companies have been very cyclical. I have the chart of their revenue and their earnings.
turns.zh: 嗯，我很熟悉这个反驳。我会说的是：从历史上看，这些公司确实非常周期性，这一点百分之百正确。我这里有一张他们收入和利润的图，

turns.en: Right. Combined going back 15 years. And it was a little bit, you know, look at a little bit of a wave, little cyclicality, but is AI a cyclical thing or a secular thing. Elon Musk thinks that he and his companies that agreed to him, they're going to need 30 times more compute than the current global capacity.
turns.zh: 对吧，合在一起可以回溯 15 年。它看起来有点像波浪，有一点周期性。但 AI 到底是一个周期性的东西，还是一个长期结构性（secular）的东西？Elon Musk 认为，他和那些同意他看法的公司，将需要比当前全球算力总量多 30 倍的算力。

turns.en: So, yes, they've been cyclical in the past. Who knows if they'll be cyclical going forward right now. They are having a secular good time. I like that. AI is a cyclical or secular. That's a good way to leave the discussion here, Kevin. It's so great to reconnect. Again, congrats on the new EMX ETF brand and the new ETF.
turns.zh: 所以，是的，他们过去是周期性的，未来会不会继续周期性，谁也说不准；但眼下，他们正处在一个结构性的美好时光里。我喜欢这个说法：AI 是周期性还是结构性，用这个来结束今天的讨论再好不过了。Kevin，太高兴又能和你聊上。再次恭喜你推出新的 EMXETF 品牌和新的 ETF。

turns.en: Certainly wishing the best of luck with those moving forward. Thank you very much for joining me. All right, Nate. Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 当然也祝你们接下来一切顺利。非常感谢你来做客。好的，Nate，谢谢你邀请我。
